lines.text: A castle that sells a monster who never lived there. A hill the Soviets bulldozed, twice. A hospital left to the forest. And a forest where a shepherd and two hundred sheep walked in... and never walked out. Four real places in Europe, partner. Stay close.
Transylvania, Romania. Bran Castle, built in the late thirteen hundreds on a rock above a mountain pass.
Every year, crowds of tourists come to see Dracula's Castle.
But Bram Stoker, who wrote Dracula in 1897, never visited Transylvania. His book doesn't mention Bran.
Vlad the Impaler, the real ruler linked to Dracula, never ruled this castle. Most historians say he never set foot inside.
Bran's real story? From 1920, it belonged to Queen Marie of Romania. Today it's a museum, full of her furniture and art.
So why Dracula's Castle? It sits on a cliff like the castle in the novel... and the legend sells tickets. Dracula never lived here. That doesn't keep people from coming to look for him.

lines.chapter: NUMBER THREE|THE HILL OF CROSSES, LITHUANIA
lines.text: Northern Lithuania. A small hill in the middle of farmland.
For generations, people have carried crosses here. For the missing, the dead, the sick.
Under Soviet rule, religion was suppressed. The hill became a quiet act of defiance.
In 1961, the authorities bulldozed it. About five thousand crosses were burned or melted down.
People came back, often at night, and planted new ones. In the 1970s the Soviets tore it down again. The crosses came back again.
In 1993, Pope John Paul the Second came to pray here. Today there are well over a hundred thousand crosses. No one knows the exact number.
Near Berlin, 1898. Work began on Beelitz Heilstatten, a sanatorium for tuberculosis patients.
It grew to about sixty buildings. One of the largest hospital complexes around Berlin.
In World War One it treated wounded soldiers. In 1916, one of them was a young corporal named Adolf Hitler.
In 1945 the Soviet army took it over. It stayed a Soviet military hospital until 1994. In 1990, East Germany's fallen leader Erich Honecker stayed here, before he was flown to Moscow.
Then most of it was abandoned. Wards, stairwells, operating rooms... left to the forest.
Locals say it's haunted. Going inside the ruins is forbidden. But today, a walkway up in the treetops lets you look down on them.
Near Cluj Napoca, Romania. The Hoia Baciu forest.
Legend says it's named after a shepherd who walked in with two hundred sheep... and was never seen again.
The trees here grow twisted and bent. And in the middle there's a clearing. An almost perfect circle, where the trees just stop.
In 1968, a military technician photographed what he said was a UFO over that clearing.
Visitors talk about strange lights, missing time, and the feeling of being watched. Today you can book night tours. Locals have their own advice. Don't go alone.
Four places. A myth, a miracle, a ruin, and a forest that keeps its secrets. Which one would you walk into after dark? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe for more files. I'll be waiting, partner.
